subject: Logistic regression: fitting many individual regressions in a single model

messages.author: 40bef15e0492270c
messages.subject: Logistic regression: fitting many individual regressions in a single model
parts:
Hi,

We are trying to fit a lot of individual logistic regression models in one go using Stan (the idea is to later add some hierarchical structure to avoid multiple testing artefacts). We are, however, running into a very serious problem, a small subset of the data (<5%, ~250k points) is taking up 19GB of RAM, regardless of using the mcmc or variational approach in cmdstan. We are not really sure why the model takes up so much memory, especially because the subset of data on disk only takes up 193MB. We are not really concerned with speed (yet), but have tried to optimise to use the least amount of memory. If we can ever get the full model with all the data to fit into memory, we will worry about speed.

The idea behind the study is there are a number of events, D, and a number of datapoints, N (in the subsetted data I am using D=255 and N= ~280k). At each data point, there is an event y (the predicted value), which takes on a discrete value from 1-255. The same event may happen at multiple data points. The idea is to model each event individually. I.e. loop over the set of unique events, setting y=1 and y=0 accordingly for each data point.

Any pointers or tips on why it is using so much memory would be much appreciated! 

I have attached a Stan script of the model. The models were built and run using the latest version of cmdstan-2.7.0.

Thanks in advance,
David

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Logistic regression: fitting many individual regressions in a single model
parts:
It's the loop in your model.

You have a D x N loop, so that's 255 * 280K = 71 million iterations, each of which
then creates an expression for theta_hat and for the bernoulli_logit that's going
to suck up lots of memory. It's basically 40 bytes or so per binary subexpression in
the model and you get around 5 per iteration, for another 200 bytes * 71 million
= 14 GB. The 19GB is almost certainly because we allocate in blocks, rather than
a byte at a time in order to ensure it only takes logarithmic time.

You could save a bit of space by turning (beta_age * age) into a dot-product and
by defining a vector of theta_hat[n] and then vectorizing bernoulli_logit, but it's
still going to take a lot of memory.

- Bob

So basically it is an intractable problem due to the data volume, even with the optimisations suggested (the final dataset would be 1200 x 80million, give or take, with about 1,5million parameters). I’ve also been considering if its actually possible to just fit the model to one event, and then use the posterior as a prior for the next model, and so forth, so I would only need to do 1x 280k iterations per model. Though I am not sure if that is actually sensible.

Thanks.

David

messages.author: 37f85c6188fe5eeb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Logistic regression: fitting many individual regressions in a single model
parts:
1200 event types with 80 million observations

It seems like you've got a different set of parameters for each event type, so why not run 1200 different Stan scripts? Of course, then you can't do partial pooling with the different events together. But instead of looking at tens of billions of bytes, you'd be looking at tens of millions, which is no problem.

And, with 80e6/1.2e3 ~ 80e3 observations per event type on average, do you really need very much prior information? If you can figure out which events are sort of "similar" instead of running 1200 scripts maybe you can cluster event types together into groups of 3 to 10 or something, running maybe 300 scripts total?

messages.author: 37f85c6188fe5eeb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Logistic regression: fitting many individual regressions in a single model
parts:
another alternative:

randomly select 20 event types and 1 million relevant data points or something like that, get the posterior distribution of the parameters from this reduced set of observations. Then fit a parametric prior for the parameters, and use it repeatedly in 1200 regressions on the remaining 79 million data points?

The point being to reduce the chance of over-fitting by gleaning some information from a subset of the data which is then used as an informed prior to regularize the individual fits to some extent. It's not as clean as the full heirarchical bayes, but it's actually do-able, so there's that going for it.

messages.author: 40bef15e0492270c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Logistic regression: fitting many individual regressions in a single model
parts:
The mode I posted was just a partial, simple model. We wanted to find out if it could be optimised to handle the very large number of sampling statements. The full model contains 2*1200 + 1200 + 1200 + 1200 + 4*1200 + 4*12 + 1200*1200 = ~1.5mil parameters. binomial_logit won't work for that, I think. 

I guess this might be one of those cases where Gibbs sampling works better, though there might be problems with convergence. 

David

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Logistic regression: fitting many individual regressions in a single model
parts:
If you can't combine observations with same probability of
success a priori, then the Bernoulli to binomial data aggregation
won't help.

I doubt Gibbs is going to work better --- it has a hard time in
high dimensions, especially with hierarchical models inducing high
posterior correlations. You can easily get fooled with Gibbs or
Metropolis into thinking you've converged if you aren't careful to
start from diffuse initializations and make sure you converge to the
same posterior means.

- Bob
